description: Sourced research on what specific companies actually test in technical interviews: loop structure, languages, SQL presence, algorithm/data-structure patterns, system design topics, difficulty calibration, and quirks. Used to target Aptivus practice packs at a user's real target employer.
legal_note: This dataset records the SHAPE of each company's interview process and the PATTERNS it draws on (e.g. 'sliding window', 'top-N per group', 'interval merging') -- never verbatim interview questions. Where a source quoted a specific question, it was paraphrased into its underlying pattern before being recorded here. No proprietary or NDA-covered question text is reproduced. All practice problems built from this dataset must be original, authored fresh from the pattern description, not reconstructed from a specific reported question. See README.md for the full legal position.

confidence_scale.high: Multiple corroborating primary sources (company engineering blog, official careers/interview-prep page, or official public handbook) confirm the claim.
confidence_scale.medium: Primary sources exist but are thin/partial, or the claim rests on multiple corroborating secondary sources (Glassdoor/Levels.fyi/interview-prep blogs) that agree with each other.
confidence_scale.low: Single weak secondary source, or sources conflict and could not be resolved.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.industry: big tech / e-commerce, cloud computing (AWS) & advertising
companies.size: ~1.56 million employees worldwide (full-time + part-time), attributed to Amazon's 2025 annual report via secondary aggregators (Demandsage, Statista); not verified directly against the 10-K

loop.summary: An asynchronous Online Assessment gates the process, followed by a virtual onsite loop (typically 4 x 55-minute rounds for SDE II) that blends coding, system design and Leadership Principles behavioral probing in every round. A Bar Raiser - a trained interviewer from outside the hiring team - sits in the loop and chairs the post-loop debrief with effective veto power. Outcome typically communicated within about 5 business days.

rounds.name: Online Assessment (OA)
rounds.covers: coding problems (~70-90 min, typically 2 questions), a Workstyles/behavioral survey aligned to Leadership Principles, and for many full-time SDE roles a ~60-minute Work Simulation scenario exercise
rounds.format: asynchronous, proctored-style integrity rules: only public non-login reference docs allowed, print-screen ends the session, copy-paste banned so code must be typed live. SDE II OA is documented as 118 min: 90 min coding + 20 min system design scenario + 8 min work style survey

rounds.name: Phone Screen
rounds.covers: coding and Leadership Principles; reported for some levels/orgs, particularly SDE I
rounds.format: video/phone; sources are conflicting on whether experienced hires go straight from OA to the loop, so this round is not universal

rounds.name: Virtual Onsite Loop Round 1-4
rounds.covers: each round blends technical assessment (coding and/or system design at scale) with 1-2 Leadership Principles probed via STAR-format behavioral questions
rounds.format: virtual, interviewers drawn from the SDE community; SDE I loops are often reported as 3 x 40-minute rounds while senior loops can run up to 5 x 60-minute rounds across multiple days

rounds.name: Bar Raiser (embedded in the loop)
rounds.covers: long-term and company-wide fit rather than team-specific fit; heavy Leadership Principles focus alongside technical assessment
rounds.format: one of the loop interviewers, not a separate stage; the Bar Raiser is an Amazon employee from any function, outside the hiring team, with extensive LP training and months of shadowing

rounds.name: Architecture Deep Dive
rounds.covers: deep architectural and design discussion for senior/principal candidates
rounds.format: additional round reported for senior+ loops only (secondary sourcing)

rounds.name: Debrief
rounds.covers: recruiter plus all interviewers convene; the Bar Raiser chairs and drives to hire/no-hire consensus and sometimes level; insufficient evidence can trigger 1-2 additional interviews before reconvening
rounds.format: post-loop meeting; outcome typically within ~5 business days

languages.notes: No primary Amazon page enumerates a fixed list - the official OA page only tells candidates to practice in the language they plan to use. The list above is broad secondary consensus. Java, Python and C++ are most common in practice. Candidates are reportedly not penalized for language choice despite Amazon's internal codebase skewing Java.

sql.notes: Query-writing SQL is not a standard part of the generalist SDE loop per multiple secondary sources. Amazon's own topics page lists 'databases' among nine general topic areas, so database concepts and data-store trade-offs can surface inside system design, but not SQL authoring. SQL is heavy in Amazon's separate Data Engineer / Data Scientist / BI Analyst tracks, which are a different job family.

system_design.notes: A dedicated system design component is confirmed from SDE II upward, appearing in both the OA (a 20-minute scenario) and the onsite loop. Amazon's own SDE II page gives the evaluation rubric explicitly: practicality, accuracy, efficiency, reliability, optimization, scalability. SDE I loops are coding- and behavioral-heavy with system design light or absent (secondary sourcing only). Senior/Principal loops add an architecture deep dive.

difficulty.notes: No primary Amazon statement of difficulty. Secondary consensus: medium-skewed with hards mixed in and occasional easies; a commonly cited SDE II shape is one medium plus one hard per coding round, with the bar described as solving solid mediums cleanly under time pressure. Reported variance across teams is significant, consistent with Amazon's team-dependent process. Sources warn that publicly tagged Amazon question sets are noisy (mixing retired OA questions and outliers).

quirks: Bar Raiser: a trained volunteer interviewer from outside the hiring team (3,600+ company-wide) who assesses long-term company fit, chairs the debrief as decision driver with effective veto power, and mentors other interviewers; program originated in 1999 as the 'Barkeeper Program'
16 Leadership Principles are woven into essentially every round rather than confined to one behavioral round; each technical interviewer typically probes 1-2 LPs via STAR stories
secondary sources argue Leadership Principles performance can outweigh raw coding performance at the debrief
Work Simulation in the OA: a ~60-minute scenario-based prioritization/triage exercise judged on LP-style reasoning, not just code correctness - distinctive to Amazon
OA integrity rules: copy-paste banned (code must be typed), print-screen ends the session, only public non-login reference docs permitted

process is explicitly team-dependent: round counts, durations and emphasis vary meaningfully by org and level
no take-home assignment; the OA is the only asynchronous component
debrief can order 1-2 additional interviews when evidence is insufficient rather than defaulting to no-hire

loop.summary: A multi-stage loop that usually runs 6-8 rounds over several weeks to a few months: recruiter screen, one or two 60-minute technical screens (coding and/or system design, sometimes using a progressive 'gate' format where one problem escalates in difficulty), often a paid ~48-hour take-home/work-trial project, then a 4-6 hour virtual (or in-person) onsite loop covering coding, system design, a technical project deep-dive/presentation, and 1-2 behavioral rounds. Loop composition varies notably by team and role -- multiple sources stress there is no single fixed template.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.covers: background, motivation, mission/AGI-safety alignment

rounds.name: Technical screen - coding
rounds.covers: coding, sometimes a progressive multi-gate problem of increasing difficulty; also occasionally an async HackerRank-style OA with 1-2 algorithmic problems (90-120 min)

rounds.name: Technical screen - system design
rounds.covers: architecture/scalability discussion, often ML-serving or infra flavored

rounds.name: Take-home / work trial
rounds.covers: self-contained practical engineering project (e.g. building a small system with retry/reliability logic), graded like production code on correctness, code quality, tests, and design decisions; reportedly compensated (~$1,000 per some public reports)
rounds.format: asynchronous, ~48-hour window (FDE roles get ~1 week plus a video walkthrough)

rounds.name: Technical deep dive
rounds.covers: defense of take-home project or a past project; tradeoffs and decisions under follow-up questioning

rounds.name: Onsite - coding
rounds.covers: implementation-heavy problems, often 'recreate behavior of an existing system' style, data-structure-from-scratch style problems
rounds.format: own IDE with screen share or shared editor

rounds.name: Onsite - system design
rounds.covers: deeper architecture round, failure modes, distributed coordination, production correctness (idempotency, retries)

rounds.name: Onsite - behavioral (leadership/collaboration)
rounds.covers: cross-functional collaboration, mission alignment, ethical judgment, conflict/collaboration scenarios; senior levels get a leadership-focused variant with a senior manager/exec

rounds.name: Domain-specific interview (optional, senior/specialist roles)
rounds.covers: deep technical expertise for ML infra, distributed systems, or safety-specific roles

permitted: any language candidate is comfortable with (commonly Python)
languages.notes: No official published language policy found; multiple secondary sources say candidates may use any language, with Python being most common given the ML-heavy codebase context. OpenAI reportedly has not published a policy on reference materials or AI-tool use during interviews, so candidates are advised to confirm with their recruiter.

sql.notes: Not a core recurring pillar, but at least one reported coding question involved implementing a subset of SQL functionality in-memory (tables, inserts, WHERE-clause selects, joins) as a systems/parsing exercise rather than a query-writing exercise. No evidence of a dedicated SQL query-writing round for the general SWE track.
